messages:
olivia_p: heads-up — brizo2b-int4 canary is hitting OOMs during short traffic spikes (~8-10 reqs/s bursts). started at 4412345000, now ~1.8% requests 500 with OOM.

sanjayk: uhoh. are these cold-starts or steady-state? any stack traces?

olivia_p: mostly mid-conversation where max_new_tokens is high. sample log: 
```
ERROR Runtime: cuda out of memory when allocating 1.18 GiB
  at torch/cuda/alloc.cu:245
  kv_cache: growth -> evict thrash at 82%
```
no obvious mem leak but fragmentation spikes when many short sessions + a few long generations.

mira: quick hypothesis: int4 quant + long KV retention + default max_new_tokens (256) -> big transient allocations. two levers: lower per-route max_new_tokens default, or shrink max_batch_size / prefetch. also check KV warmup/prefetch heuristics.

olivia_p: i reproduced locally on a dev node with CI image. canary config is: 
```
route: /v/generate/brizo2b
defaults:
  max_new_tokens: 256
  max_batch_size: 8
  prefetch_percent: 20
  kv_keep_recent: true
```
changing batch to 4 reduces OOMs in my runs. but want an ops-safe rollout plan.

mira: re: quality — ran a small eval on our convo-regset after int4 quant. avg EM dropped by ~2.3% vs fp16 on long-turn prompts (>150 tokens). short prompts unaffected. We should either:
- keep int4 but restrict default max_new_tokens to 128 for public route, or
- enable int8 fallback for hot paths (costly)

olivia_p: can we do a quick policy change to limit defaults for the canary population? patch that in console will be fastest.

tariq: +1 to lowering defaults. operationally i'd also bump the kv-eviction-threshold and enable a soft cap on KV per-session to avoid thrash. proposed changes:
```
- defaults.max_new_tokens: 128
- defaults.max_batch_size: 4
- prefetch_percent: 10
- kv_eviction_delta: 0.15   # raise eviction aggressiveness when mem > 70%
- hot_route_fallback: int8 for requests > 200 tokens
```
we can do canary config change + monitor 30m then promote.

sanjayk: quick deployment note: in console the route-level defaults are JSON. patch via api: 
```
PATCH /api/routes/brizo2b
{ "defaults": { "max_new_tokens": 128, "max_batch_size": 4 }}
```
I'll queue the patch and set a 15-min canary window with auto-rollback on >0.5% error increase.

deploy-bot: Canary patch applied to route /v/generate/brizo2b by sanjayk. Monitoring for 15m.

olivia_p: after the patch i re-ran the burst test: errors dropped to 0.2%, latency p95 improved ~60ms. good win.

mira: for the quality regression, i'll run a focused quant-calibration (KL temp sweep + activation scaling) and compare. If that yields <1% drop we can relax fallback. I’ll have results in ~4 hours.

tariq: follow-ups
- mira: run calibration and post metrics to the eval dashboard (owner)
- sanjayk: keep canary for 1h, then promote if error stable
- olivia_p: add a short doc in the onboarding checklist about defaulting to 128 max_new_tokens for int4 variants and conservative batch sizes

olivia_p: tagging @tariq @mira for visibility, thanks all :thumbsup:

mira: noted. starting calibration job now (job id: brizo2b-cal-4412). will link eval diff when ready.

deploy-bot: Canary monitoring complete — no auto-rollback triggered at 15m.

olivia_p: marking this thread as actionable. will update if any regressions show up after wider rollout.
